predecessors.note: 'Around the year of 1084' Zvenyhorod, Terebovlia and Peremyshl were founded within the Principality of Volhynia (page, paraphrased); Volodar Rostyslavych received Zvenyhorod. Cliopatria starts its Terebovlia row in 1085 and its Peremyshl row in 1056.

land.text: the principality of Zvenyhorod 'in the west of modern Ukraine', capital Zvenyhorod

successors.note: 'In 1141 the principality united with' Peremyshl and Terebovlia. The Halych dossier (eu-16-d) enters Zvenyhorod as a gain in 1145, after Ivan Berladnyk's bid; the two dossiers differ by four years.

capitals.note: Coordinates are Lviv's, as an approximation: Zvenyhorod has no gazetteer entry and the page gives none.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row). The page gives no area and no boundary, only 'in the west of modern Ukraine' with the capital at Zvenyhorod; a 50 km radius round Lviv is my reading. Cliopatria's Peremyshl (from 1056) and Terebovlia (from 1085) shapes may already cover this ground: the renderer must resolve the overlap.

region.text: the principality of Zvenyhorod 'in the west of modern Ukraine', capital Zvenyhorod

ledger.note: c. 1084: Zvenyhorod is founded as the appanage of Volodar Rostyslavych. 'Around the year of 1084' Zvenyhorod, Terebovlia and Peremyshl were founded within the Principality of Volhynia; 'Zvenyhorod went to Volodar Rostyslavych, others to his brothers'. The page says 'around'; the year is its own, the land my reading.

region.text: the principality of Zvenyhorod 'in the west of modern Ukraine', capital Zvenyhorod

ledger.note: 1141: Zvenyhorod merges into the Principality of Halych. 'In 1141 the principality united with' Peremyshl and Terebovlia (the page does not name the union; the Peremyshl and Terebovlia dossiers call it the Principality of Halych).

certainty.note: No boundary on the page; a radius round the capital.

sources.note: Fragmentary article: c. 1084 founding within Volhynia, Volodar Rostyslavych, 1141 union, 1239 Horde, 1350/1392 Poland; no infobox, area or princes years.

notes: New state flagged by eu-16-d (Halych, which enters Zvenyhorod as a gain in 1145). One page only (page budget; the article is fragmentary and its text shows no infobox). Not settled: the end year (this page 1141; the Halych dossier 1145, from the Ivan Berladnyk episode), the extent (no page gives it), the princes (only Volodar Rostyslavych is named). Capital coordinates are Lviv's as an approximation. The page's lead and history differ on 1350 vs 1392 for Poland, which is outside this state's life. Wikidata id unknown.
